sections.heading: The Five VAPT Phases
items: Phase 1 — Scoping: Define in-scope targets, testing objectives, constraints, emergency contacts. Sign scope document + RoE + authorization letter. OUTPUT: Legal framework for the engagement
Phase 2 — Reconnaissance: Passive OSINT (WHOIS, DNS, Shodan, LinkedIn, Certificate Transparency) + active recon (within scope). OUTPUT: Target profile
Phase 3 — Scanning & Enumeration: Port scanning, service detection, vulnerability scanning, service enumeration. OUTPUT: Structured vulnerability list
Phase 4 — Exploitation: Controlled exploitation of confirmed vulnerabilities; privilege escalation; lateral movement assessment. OUTPUT: Exploitation notes with evidence
Phase 5 — Reporting: Executive summary + detailed findings + remediation guidance. OUTPUT: Professional report — the deliverable

sections.heading: PTES — Penetration Testing Execution Standard (7 Phases)
items: 1. Pre-engagement Interactions — Scoping, contracts, authorisation
2. Intelligence Gathering — Reconnaissance; OSINT and active recon
3. Threat Modelling — Identify likely attackers, assets at risk, attack vectors
4. Vulnerability Analysis — Vulnerability discovery and validation
5. Exploitation — Confirmed exploitation within scope
6. Post-Exploitation — Privilege escalation, lateral movement, data discovery
7. Reporting — Findings documentation and remediation guidance

sections.heading: Scope Document vs Rules of Engagement
items: Scope Document = WHAT: In-scope targets, out-of-scope items, testing objectives, constraints, authorisation statement
Rules of Engagement = HOW: Testing window, permitted/prohibited techniques, escalation protocol, communication cadence, data handling

sections.heading: Finding Severity Ratings
items: Critical (CVSS 9.0–10.0): Immediate exploitation, severe business impact — e.g., unauthenticated RCE, SQL injection on production database
High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): Serious risk, likely exploitable — e.g., authentication bypass, privilege escalation to admin
Medium (CVSS 4.0–6.9): Moderate risk, requires conditions — e.g., CSRF, information disclosure, weak session management
Low (CVSS 0.1–3.9): Minor risk, difficult to exploit — e.g., unnecessary service exposure, weak cipher support
Informational (CVSS 0): No direct exploitability, best practice gap — e.g., missing security headers, verbose error messages

sections.heading: Professional Report — Required Sections
items: Executive Summary — Non-technical, for CISO/CEO/board. Overall risk rating, critical findings in business terms, strategic recommendations
Scope & Methodology — What was tested, when, how, and what was excluded (with reference to signed scope document)
Findings Summary — Risk matrix showing finding counts by severity level
Detailed Findings — Per vulnerability: title, severity, CVSS, affected system, description, evidence, steps to reproduce, remediation guidance
Appendices — Raw tool output, credentials used, tool versions

sections.heading: Passive vs Active Reconnaissance
items: Passive: Public sources, no direct target contact — WHOIS, DNS records, Shodan, LinkedIn, job postings, Certificate Transparency, Google Dorks
Active: Direct target interaction (requires authorisation) — DNS zone transfer, port scan, banner grabbing, web spidering
